Anya: quick follow-up from the multi-region RFC — we need a concrete contract for sticky sessions vs legal locality. specifically: when are we allowed to move a session off-region? :eyes:
Julian: legal says EU_ONLY sessions can never leave eu without explicit consent. so affinity must be strict unless tenant opts in.
Mike: right. RFC had lease-based affinity but that doesn't cover cached PII in the KV layer. replication of PII is a no-go.
Sophie: proposal: add session-scope flags: `ephemeral`, `cross-region-allowed`, `pii-prohibited`. routing layer enforces constraints.
Tara: how do we expose that to customers? API example: `POST /sessions { residency: \"EU_ONLY\", consent: false }`
Leo: prototype routing header we discussed: `X-Redwood-ResStamp: eu-west-1:stamp123`
Leo: sample policy JSON:
```json
{
  "session_id": "s-abc",
  "residency": "EU_ONLY",
  "flags": ["pii-prohibited"],
  "lease_ttl_s": 30
}
```
InfraBot: deploybot: canary started for proxy-affinity-fix on infra/staging (build 2026.03.18-9) :rocket:
Anya: main open questions: 1) active/active writes — do we allow dual-writes for session-scoped state? 2) safe handoff steps when a lease expires or region goes down.
Julian: avoid dual-writes for anything with residency constraints. single-writer lease is simpler and auditable.
Mike: agree. handoff sketch: 1) target region acquires provisional lease from control plane, 2) source region marks session as draining, 3) prefix KV cache shadow-copies non-PII, 4) final lease swap, 5) confirm and release.
Mike: pseudo sequence (very rough):
```
acquire_provisional(dest, session)
source.mark_draining(session)
shadow_copy_nonpii(source, dest)
swap_lease(source, dest)
confirm_activate(dest, session)
```
Sophie: operationally this will add latency on failover. suggestion: warm standby + shadow writes for cross-region-allowed sessions so cutover is near-instant. for EU_ONLY we keep strict approach.
Tara: legal needs audit trail for every cross-region transfer: who requested, timestamp, justification. also retention of residency stamps in logs.
Anya: consent model: tenants can set `residency: EU_ONLY` (block transfer) or `residency: PREFER_LOCAL` (allow transfer on outage) or `residency: ANY` (free). add explicit `consent` flag for end-user opt-ins.
Leo: implementation risk = cache divergence and race on lease TTL. mitigation: use monotonic lease epoch + versioned tombstones for prefixes. on access, reconcile + migrate.
Mike: cache eviction pattern: tombstone with `migrated_at` header, and `migrate_on_read` path for background reconciliation.
Sophie: long-term refactor idea: push session affinity decisions into the edge (gateway) with lightweight hinting headers. gateway keeps cookie with region-stamp and fallback policy. this centralizes routing and reduces per-service complexity.
Julian: this requires the gateway to be residency-aware and to surface traces to compliance. not small but cleaner boundaries.
Tara: legal also needs an API to query session history per customer (for audits). add `GET /sessions/:id/history` to the data contract.
Anya: ok action items: Julian to draft the lease-state machine and failure scenarios, Leo to prototype `X-Redwood-ResStamp` and migrate-on-read logic, Tara to coordinate with legal on required audit fields, Mike to write the handoff sequence and tombstone format, Sophie to sketch gateway hinting refactor. I'll open a follow-up RFC linking these pieces. :+1:
Julian: noted, I'll start a doc with state transitions and edge cases.
Mike: will prototype tombstone payload and a small sim for race conditions.
Leo: will wire up header proof-of-concept in the proxy canary environment.

Anya: thanks everyone — expect the RFC link tomorrow. :wave:
